---
id: "smk-08"
title: "Rust (programming language)"
---

Rust is a systems programming language that focuses on memory safety, concurrency and performance. It began as a personal project of Graydon Hoare in 2006 and was sponsored by Mozilla from 2009; the first stable release, Rust 1.0, appeared in 2015. Rust achieves memory safety without a garbage collector through an ownership system: every value has a single owner, references are checked by a borrow checker at compile time, and data races are prevented by the type system. The language has algebraic data types, pattern matching, traits for polymorphism and a macro system. Programs are compiled ahead of time by the rustc compiler, which uses LLVM as its back end, and dependencies are managed by the Cargo build tool and the crates.io registry. Rust is used for operating system components, web browsers, command-line tools and embedded software, and it has been adopted in the Linux kernel.
